cases.claim: Reference Compass Search 1.0 can evaluate objectives without access to gradients.
Reference Compass Search 1.0 reduces its exploration radius after every step.
Reference Compass Search 1.0 uses less memory than Adaptive Beacon Search 2.0.
Adaptive Compass Search 2.0 halves its radius after two stagnant steps.
Adaptive Compass Search 2.0 leaves its radius unchanged after two stagnant steps.
Adaptive Compass Search 2.0 outperforms Reference Compass Search 1.0 on a thirty-dimensional benchmark.
Grid Ribbon 1.0 was validated for bounded continuous problems in dimension 10.
The Grid Ribbon 1.0 validation included integer variables.
Grid Ribbon 1.0 restarted whenever it encountered a nonfinite objective.
The listed implementation of Scaled Grid Ribbon 1.1 applies this variant's scaling.
Scaled Grid Ribbon 1.1 and Grid Ribbon 1.0 describe the same variant.
The implementation fixture:grid:ScaledV11 returned a verified solution.
Adaptive Beacon Search 2.0 counts initialization against the function evaluation budget.
Adaptive Beacon Search 2.0 excludes initialization from its evaluation budget.
Adaptive Beacon Search 2.0 has an exact implementation in the fixture catalog.
The Adaptive Beacon Search 2.0 ablation had a higher median score than the original variant in this minimization test.
The Adaptive Beacon Search 2.0 ablation had a lower median score than the original variant in this test.
The experiment demonstrates the original Adaptive Beacon Search 2.0 is globally optimal.
Reflective Optics 3.0 uses reflective bound repair.
Reflective Optics 3.0 discards points outside the bounds without repair.
Reflective Optics 3.0 was run using the fixture:optics:ReflectiveV3 implementation.
The controlled fixture trial trial-beacon-1 consumed 500 function evaluations.
The controlled fixture trial trial-beacon-1 stopped after 250 function evaluations.
The same fixture run proves Adaptive Beacon Search 2.0 is optimal for noisy objectives.
